page: Amazon Web Services c7gd.metal is a bare-metal, compute-optimized server powered by 64 physical cores of the 64-bit ARMv8 AWS Graviton Neoverse-V1 processor. Operating at 2.6 GHz with one thread per core, this dedicated hardware configuration is paired with 128.0 GB of DDR5 memory, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per core. The server includes 3800 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 30 Gbps. No graphics processing units are present on this instance.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core capabilities, with stress-ng multi-core performance scoring 98061.21 and Geekbench multi-core reaching a top-tier score of 20998.0. Software compilation with Clang also registers in the top tier at 59925.0. Memory bandwidth is a notable strength, with read-only small block cached speeds at 6191.89 GB/sec and uncached large block write speeds at 121.15 GB/sec. Database operations and key-value stores perform well, as evidenced by a strong PassMark database score of 31581.65 and Redis SET operations reaching 102.32 million operations per second. However, single-core metrics, such as the Geekbench single-core score of 1544.0, and text generation for small LLM models represent performance bottlenecks.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c7gd.metal offers high resource density by combining dedicated bare-metal ARM cores with a substantial 3800 GB local NVMe SSD. This eliminates the overhead of virtualization and external storage latency, making it a viable option for workloads requiring high-throughput local storage and parallelized compute. Suitable workloads include multi-threaded software compilation, database hosting, static web serving, and parallelized physics simulations.
